But requirement includes promotion from associate professor to professor in 2022 at same university where undergrad/graduate degrees. None supported. Could be partially_supported because at least substantive part: Indian author and associate professor? The requirement's material parts: There is Indian author; got promoted from associate professor to professor in 2022; at same university where did UG and grad degrees. Claims establish Indian author/associate professor at University of Delhi maybe. Does that count as substantive material part? Yes "There is an Indian author" and "associate professor" partly. But "got promoted..." unsupported. So partially_supported? Need consider "There is an Indian author" is part of R1. C1 supports Indian author. But maybe this is just entity mention? It states she is author and associate professor at India. So partially.

R2: "They had pursued their PhD abroad at a Canadian university under the guidance of an Iranian professor." C2 says she pursued PhD in Mathematics at Dalhousie University, Canada. Supports PhD abroad at Canadian university. Does not support under guidance of Iranian professor. Partially_supported.

R3: "who dreamt of becoming a writer but switched to mathematics at the end of high school and got their doctorate in Minnesota." This refers to Iranian professor. Claims none mention Iranian professor, dream writer, switched to math, doctorate Minnesota. Unsupported.

R4: "The author published a book connecting mathematics to an ancient technique for liberation 20 years after completing their PhD." C1 says author of The Secret World of Vipassana and Mathematics (2016), book exploring singularity between Vipassana and Mathematics. Vipassana is ancient technique? Claim says Vipassana and Mathematics. That supports published a book connecting mathematics to Vipassana (an ancient technique for liberation?) The claim states "exploring singularity between Vipassana and Mathematics." Vipassana is an ancient technique? The claim doesn't explicitly say "ancient technique for liberation"; but likely. Requirement also "20 years after completing their PhD". C2 says pursued PhD, no completion date. C1 gives publication date 2016. No PhD completion date. So cannot establish 20 years after. Partially_supported if book connection established. Need material part: book connecting mathematics to ancient technique for liberation. C1 establishes book connecting Vipassana and Mathematics. Does it establish "ancient technique for liberation"? It doesn't state Vipassana is ancient technique for liberation. But maybe "Vipassana" is known as ancient meditation technique? We cannot use outside knowledge. The claim only says "book exploring the singularity between Vipassana and Mathematics." The requirement's phrase "ancient technique for liberation" may refer to Vipassana? Without outside knowledge, no. But C1 names "The Secret World of Vipassana and Mathematics" and "singularity between Vipassana and Mathematics." It does not define Vipassana. However, "ancient technique for liberation" may be exactly Vipassana? The claim doesn't say. The task skeleton mentions "ancient technique for liberation" but no verified claim states Vipassana is that. So support for book connecting math to ancient technique maybe not fully. But at least "published a book connecting mathematics to Vipassana" and 2016 date. Do we count as substantive part? Maybe yes, "published a book connecting mathematics to [Vipassana]" if we infer Vipassana from original? But cannot use outside. Yet original question uses "ancient technique for liberation" maybe to identify Vipassana? Hmm.

We can only use claims. C1 says book exploring singularity between Vipassana and Mathematics. It doesn't say Vipassana is ancient technique for liberation. But the phrase "Vipassana" itself could be considered ancient technique? No outside knowledge. The claim states "a book exploring the singularity between Vipassana and Mathematics." If "Vipassana" is a term, it's not established as "ancient technique for liberation." But maybe a verified claim can implicitly establish? No.

Need decide statuses. For R4, at least establishes published a book connecting mathematics to Vipassana, but not ancient technique for liberation nor 20 years after PhD. So partially_supported? If "Vipassana and Mathematics" is close enough to "mathematics to an ancient technique for liberation" because Vipassana is presumably ancient technique? The instruction says do not use outside knowledge. However, the claim itself says "Vipassana" but not its nature. So not fully. Partially at least publication of book. So partially_supported.

R5: "then published a journal article on a similar topic six years after publishing the book." No claims about journal article or similar topic. Unsupported.

R6: "What is the title of that article?" This is the ultimate question. It requires the title of the article. Claims don't provide any article title. Unsupported.

Need be careful: R6 is not a factual requirement? It's question. In skeleton, requirement is "What is the title of that article?" Status? We evaluate if claims establish title. No. Unsupported, supported_by empty.

Need output JSON only. Ensure each requirement_id exactly once. Provide statuses and supported_by claim IDs.

Need maybe R1 fully? Let's scrutinize possible status for R1. Requirement: "There is an Indian author who got promoted from associate professor to professor in 2022 at the same university where they did their undergraduate and graduate degrees."

C1: Alka Marwaha is an associate professor of Mathematics at Jesus and Mary College, University of Delhi, India, and author of book. Does "associate professor" at Jesus and Mary College, University of Delhi, India establish "Indian author"? She is at Indian institution, author. It doesn't say Indian nationality, but likely "Indian author" means author from India? It says at University of Delhi, India. It supports "Indian author" maybe. But "got promoted from associate professor to professor in 2022" not supported. "same university where they did undergrad and graduate degrees" not supported. So partial.

R2: C2 supports PhD at Dalhousie University Canada. No Iranian professor. Partial.

R3: Unsupported.

R4: C1 supports book connecting mathematics and Vipassana. Does it support "20 years after completing PhD"? No. Also "ancient technique for liberation" maybe not exact. Partial. If we decide C1 doesn't establish "ancient technique for liberation", then only supports "published a book connecting mathematics to Vipassana" but not the required ancient technique. Still substantive? The requirement is a book connecting mathematics to an ancient technique for liberation 20 years after completing PhD. C1 gives book title and topic. It connects math to Vipassana. The term Vipassana might be the ancient technique. But no explicit. I'd mark partial.

R5 unsupported.

R6 unsupported.

Need final JSON with no extra.
